settings._comment: skillDir lists every skill whose domCheckIntervalMs you want to vary: customer_front_desk (the sidebar new-message DETECTOR) + the rt_chat_bot* RESPONDERS (one chat_message_added monitor per tab). Adjust this list to match the responders your run actually starts (see the [BrowserAutomation] Parsed ... skill=rt_chat_botNN lines in runlogs/eCan.log). readyMarkerCount=1 waits for the first monitor (the detector) to go live; do NOT set it to the tab count. emulation knob names match emulation_config.json (renderer/dom/focus/send/llmFault/...).

rounds._comment: A/B BASELINE for detection_blackout (run this round FIRST). IDENTICAL ramp + DOM + churn as detection_blackout, with the ONLY difference being scrapeStall.enabled=false — so the eCan scrapes stay fast no matter how large the threads grow. EXPECT in results/<run>_detection.json: max detection_lag < ~35s, starvation_windows = 0, high_lag_in_starvation = 0. Any deviation here means the ramp/churn alone (not the scrape stall) is causing lag and the next round's result would be confounded.
rounds.name: detection_blackout_clean

rounds._comment: mt070 detection-blackout repro (2026-06-03). 6 customers join over 6 min, each then sends a follow-up every 30s for ~10 min so per-customer threads grow. The load-dependent scrapeStall makes every eCan scrape Runtime.evaluate busy-wait proportional to accumulated messages + concurrent customers, so once the threads have grown the scrapes cross the 6s detection-timeout cliff and the sidebar detector goes blind for 100s+. EXPECT in results/<run>_detection.json: max detection_lag >> 100s, starvation_windows > 0, several high_lag_in_starvation. Compare against the detection_blackout_clean baseline (scrapeStall off, run just before) where max lag stays < ~35s.
rounds.name: detection_blackout
